issue.title: [Feature Proposal] Four-Layer Mesh Architecture: BLE + LoRa + Tor + Nostr for Global Resilient Network
issue.body:
Problem

BitChat currently works well in dense urban areas where many users have the app installed. However, the network dies wherever user density drops. A single user in a city cannot receive messages if there's no chain of BitChat nodes around them — even if millions of phones with Bluetooth are physically present.

## Proposed Architecture

Four layers working together as one system:

```
Layer 1 — Local (no internet, no infrastructure)
BLE mesh: phone → phone, ~300m radius
Already in BitChat ✅

Layer 2 — Regional (no internet, hardware relay)
LoRa via Meshtastic: relay → relay, up to 10km
Already exists in Meshtastic ✅
BitChat → Meshtastic integration: partial ✅

Layer 3 — Anonymous global backbone (when internet available)
Tor → Nostr relays → other continent
Already in BitChat ✅

Layer 4 — Passive background relay
BLE advertiser/scanner running as Android foreground service
Starts on boot, invisible to user, minimal battery via BLE low power mode
NOT YET IMPLEMENTED ❌
```

## The Key Insight

Layers 1, 2, and 3 already exist in BitChat or in compatible open source projects. The missing piece is **Layer 4** — an always-on background relay that turns every installed device into an automatic node without the user actively opening the app.

This is architecturally similar to how Apple's Find My works — every device passively participates in relaying packets using a registered BLE UUID, without user interaction.

## Prior Art — COVID Exposure Notifications

This architecture has already been proven at global scale. During COVID-19, Apple and Google implemented the Exposure Notifications system which:

- Ran on **every iOS and Android device** without user interaction
- Used **BLE Advertisement with a registered UUID** (`0xFD6F`) at OS level
- Each device passively scanned and rebroadcast tokens in background
- Required **zero user action** after initial permission grant
- Consumed **minimal battery** via BLE low power mode

The technical mechanism is identical to what Layer 4 proposes. The difference:

| COVID EN | BitChat Layer 4 |
|---|---|
| Centralized — tokens sent to Apple/Google servers | Decentralized — packets relayed peer to peer |
| Single purpose — exposure detection | General purpose — message relay |
| Built into OS by Apple/Google | Implemented as always-on foreground service |
| Requires OS partnership | Works with public BLE API available to any app |

**The COVID system proved that BLE-based passive relay works reliably on billions of devices simultaneously.** BitChat can achieve the same relay behaviour using the same public BLE APIs — without requiring OS-level integration.

## Implementation Suggestion for Layer 4 (Android)

```kotlin
// 1. Register custom UUID for passive relay
val BITCHAT_RELAY_UUID = UUID.fromString("YOUR-UUID-HERE")

// 2. Boot receiver — start relay on device boot
class BootReceiver : BroadcastReceiver() {
    override fun onReceive(context: Context, intent: Intent) {
        if (intent.action == Intent.ACTION_BOOT_COMPLETED) {
            context.startForegroundService(
                Intent(context, BitchatRelayService::class.java)
            )
        }
    }
}

// 3. Passive relay logic
// Scan for packets with BITCHAT_RELAY_UUID
// If hop counter < MAX_HOPS → rebroadcast and forget
// No storage, no logging, pure relay
```

## Result

Once critical mass is reached in a region — the network becomes impossible to shut down without physically removing every device. No servers. No central point of failure. Works during protests, blackouts, natural disasters.

The four layers together mean:
- **Local coverage** — BLE between phones
- **City/regional coverage** — LoRa relays
- **Cross-continent** — Tor + Nostr when internet is available
- **Always on** — passive background relay, zero user interaction required

## Known Vulnerability — Timing Attack & Physical Triangulation

This architecture has a fundamental privacy weakness that must be acknowledged.

**The problem:**

Any party that controls multiple nodes in the network can measure latency between hops and calculate physical distance between devices. With three controlled nodes — full triangulation of a user's physical location is possible. No encryption is broken. No messages are read. Just timing.

```
Attacker controls Node A, Node B, Node C
↓
Measures time: A→B, B→C, A→C
↓
Calculates physical distance via speed of BLE signal
↓
Triangulates exact location of target device
```

**This means:**

- BitChat protects **message content** via end-to-end encryption ✅
- BitChat does **NOT** protect **physical presence** in the network ❌
- BitChat does **NOT** protect **physical location** of the user ❌

For a journalist at a protest — authorities don't need to read messages. They only need to know the journalist was there. Timing metadata is enough.

**Tor partially solves this** by adding artificial delays and onion routing — but only for the internet layer (Layer 3). The local BLE mesh (Layer 1) remains fully exposed to this attack.

**Proposed mitigations:**

1. **Random relay delay** — each node waits a random 0–500ms before rebroadcasting, destroying timing precision
2. **Dummy packets** — nodes periodically broadcast empty packets to create noise in timing analysis
3. **MAC address rotation** — already partially implemented, needs to be enforced on every advertisement packet

This vulnerability is not unique to BitChat — it exists in every mesh protocol including Meshtastic, goTenna, and others. But it must be documented and mitigated especially for high-risk users.

## References
- Apple Find My network architecture
- Google/Apple Exposure Notifications API specification
- Meshtastic LoRa protocol

comment.body:
I found this issue after [posting about benchmark at Reddit](https://www.reddit.com/r/bitchat/comments/1t9ngv2/any_benchmark_in_different_scenarios/). 300m sounds like a really far distance already. 

[In my bold dream](https://www.reddit.com/r/bluetooth/comments/1scppn0/any_social_app_like_this/), it could pickup messages from a car that's passing you on the highway, say within 25m range. Assuming the relative speed is 5km/hr, rough math: 25m/5km/hr = 0.005*3600 second = 18s, even with 25km/hr it gives 3.6s, which I assume sufficient time to get connected and deliver multiple messages.

Curios if anyones tested that and other scenarios, like in a moving bus or train or even plane?

issue.title: Feat: Walkie Talkie Mode via Mesh BT
issue.body:
Real-time voice (PTT/walkie-talkie): Opus/Speex at 8–24 kbps, 16 kHz mono. Feasible over 1 hop; 2+ hops adds latency and loss.

  Add Push‑to‑Talk UI and recorder
•  Add a mic/hold-to-talk button in Views/ContentView.swift; wire to existing bitchat/Services/VoiceRecorder.swift (16 kHz mono, ~16–24 kbps).
•  Define a new Noise payload type (NoisePayloadType.voiceFrame) and a simple VoiceFrame header (streamId, seq, ts, codec).
•  ChatViewModel routes start/stop events and toggles speaker playback.
•  Low‑latency streaming over the mesh
•  In bitchat/Services/BLEService.swift, implement a prioritized “VoiceStreamSender” that batches 20 ms frames into ~200 ms chunks, fragments them, and sends with TTL=1–2 and deterministic subset fanout.
•  Use BinaryProtocol v2 framing for larger chunks; carry frames inside MessageType.noiseEncrypted with payload type voiceFrame.
